reviews.x: My son has sensory integration disorder that makes tooth brushing difficult for him.  He constantly gags and bites on his toothbrush.  His pediatric dentist recommended this toothbrush, and it really works!  It makes brushing his teeth much easier.  Because the bristles wrap around his tooth, we are able to get all surfaces of his teeth clean.  I definitely recommend this toothbrush!  It has made a huge difference for my son!

reviews.t: Interesting. Takes some getting used to,
reviews.x: I was curious, so these became stocking stuffers this Christmas.  Of course, Santa put one in my stocking as well.  I love the idea behind the design and I've wondered many times why toothbrushes weren't made in a shape like this.  Then I found these, and I thought, "finally!".  But, as cool as they are, it's hard to maneuver in your mouth. The end tip is wide, to accommodate the wrap around bristles, and when I brush (and other family members) the large end tip hits into your back gums when you

My Son who lives with Autism and is highly sensitive to various tactile stimulations. dragging a brush across his teeth can be incredibly uncomfortable for him.  this brush helps him get the just done efficiently. this is the best tooth brush design ever!

reviews.x: I bought these for my 2 children with autism and I love them! My children aren't particularly fond of brushing their teeth and usually won't tolerate more than 30 seconds of brushing. With these I can brush all the surfaces of their teeth within that time and feel satisfied that they've gotten the cleaning they need. reviews.t: I love the way it works on my teeth but doesn't ...
reviews.x: On the fence about these. Originally bought for my toddlers but I didn't pay attention to the dimensions since my search was "toddler toothbrush" so I just assumed they would be small enough for them. Nope, they're adult size. No biggie. Just thought I'd use them myself.  I love the way it works on my teeth but doesn't clean gums or tongue. reviews.t: I wish I had found these years ago!
reviews.x: If you struggle with performing oral hygiene on another person, you will love these toothbrushes.  The multi-sided bristles mean you can clean more effectively in much less time.  This is very helpful for situations where the recipient is uncooperative.  I recommend these!

reviews.t: Poor excuse for the real thing.
reviews.x: This is a very poor quality "Made in China" knock-off of the Benefit  toothbrush made by Benedent. I have used the Benefit brushes for years and like them very well, but these are cheap imposters. The bristles are too short to reach the gum line and after just a single brushing they were already fraying. I am returning them for a refund and have already placed my order with Dental Depot for the real McCoy where I always used to purchase them. They have a variety of handles designed for c

reviews.t: Great for kids with special needs!
reviews.x: I work with a lot of kids and adults with special needs and also have a sister who has Angelman's Syndrome. About 99% of the individuals I work with HATE oral care and fight against it every step of the way. I have used these toothbrushes with many of my clients and just recently purchased some for my sister. I'm so pleased with them!  First, it is much easier to get these toothbrushes into their mouths, which are usually almost clamped shut. Second, it is much easier to move them around the mou
I wasn't sure about these but thought, what the heck.  I am amazed at how much cleaner they get my son's teeth.  Even his dentist was impressed! =)

reviews.t: Wonderful brush for special needs kids and their parents
reviews.x: I purchased these for my special needs son who isn't able to brush his own teeth yet. I can't begin to say how wonderful these toothbrushes are! I will never use anything else. I struggled getting the backs of his teeth because he squirms so much and doesn't like having them brushed so it took forever to get all sides. He kept having cavities and the dentist made me feel like the worst mom ever for allowing my special needs child to have cavities. Well I was brushing them and I thought thoroughl

I bought these toothbrushes to make an already difficult process easier with my toddler.  I can't understand why my toddler has to fight teeth brushing every single time, twice a day for as long as he has had teeth!  But that's another story.  These toothbrushes, in theory, are great.  They surround the tooth and make brushing a bit faster.  HOWEVER, children, and particularly toddlers, do not behave like adults (something the manufacturer did not consider).  They do not understand yet to spit o

My 3 year old cannot brush by herself yet but with this brush she can get started and I can finish the job without accidentally stabbing the inside of her cheek. What a great invention. It doesn't just save time, the teeth become like a guide for the brush and hand so it helps with getting a feel for brushing.
Concept was good.  However, I found bristles were too short to adequately clean at the gum line, where many cavities form.  I would recommend to only those with very short teeth.

I thought this would be good for my son with autism and cut his time brushing.  My 8yo Aspie loves it.  However, my older boy with more fine motor issues has more trouble using it.  We went back to a regular toothbrush for him.

reviews.t: fun ones you decorate with stickers
reviews.x: I purchased these for my son, who due to his sensory issues, HATES having his teeth brushed.  I've tried electrics, fun ones you decorate with stickers, favorite characters, etc.  He just hates it.  So I figured that I have to make the most of the time I have to brush his teeth, and looked for a surround-like toothbrush that would let me access as much of his teeth/gums as possible in a short time.  I feel better about using this as opposed to a standard toothbrush.  I kept one for myself and it

I'm fanatic about my son's dental hygiene because he is special needs & I'd hate for him to have toothaches or problems. My son is 7 & these do what they claim to do. However, the bristles are a mite too short & it makes me wonder if it reaches far enough. No gums stimulation, that's for sure. I expect that he'd outgrow them once his baby teeth are gone. These are sized mainly for children & still yet again I'd say, the bristles are too short for the sides.  Updated: Amazon sent me the wrong pro

In a rush (my own fault) I bought Surround Toothbrushes by mistake.  They just do not work.  I (carefully) ordered DenTrust brushes again, and now feel clean. reviews.t: Perfect for all, but especially helpful for those with sensory issues.
reviews.x: I purchased these for my son with autism.  He has sensory issues (sounds, tastes, touching sensations) and doesn't enjoy having his teeth brushed.  Because the brush surrounds his teeth, I'm able to get the brushing done in much less time.  These work very well for him and his needs due to his sensitivity.  Pros: - The handles are nice and sturdy, with a powered rubberized feeling. - There are nodules on the handle to help with grip as well. - Each brush comes with a plastic cap for storage/trav

I wanted this to be super awesome, and the concept is great.  But this is like the hardest bristle I have ever used.  Definitely not soft.  Definitely not even medium.  I used mine for a couple of days, but switched back to my spin brush type toothbrush.  This just shredded my gums.  If this were available in a softer bristle, I would definitely buy them.  Great concept, though.  Hanging on to mine as a backup brush.

What kid really like brushing their teeth? Not mine thats for sure but these brushes make sure that while they are hating life, they are atleast brushing all the areas. My husband and I like ours too. Awesome for smaller children. Makes brushing our 2 year old easier and quicker before he starts his full blown world ending tantrum.

I tried these for my special needs child, as brushing his teeth is hard enough, and they reach more around the teeth. My only complaint would be that they only come in soft, and that makes the bristles wear out faster. Having to go through the toothbrushes monthly makes it costly, as they are not that cheap for only four.

reviews.t: Best toothbrush ever even for adults
reviews.x: Best toothbrush ever even for adults!!!! Omg!!! Why didn't I see this before now!!!!! I got it for myself and It cleans so well and you don't need to apply so much pressure, literally it does magic and your teeth comes out not only feeling fresh in and out but also plaque free and sparkling!!! I highly recommend!

Good quality materials. The softer bushes are gentle on one's gums, yet sturdy enough to do an incredibly thorough job cleaning teeth. reviews.t: The mouth is the window to the body...
reviews.x: Dental hygiene is so important to me. I make sure to teach my kids as well. One was diagnosed with ASD and he was very fidgety when it was brushing teeth time. They both enjoy which is a huge plus and it cuts the time to brush! I would love this if I was a child. Brush, floss, rinse, done!

reviews.t: Works as well as that other brand - and has bristles.
reviews.x: This works just fine.  The other brand uses plastic "icicles" to form the brush. Onlt thing i miss about those is the sharpness of the handle (it can be used to scrape the back of the tongue) and the built in tongue scraper.

claims.text: Many reviewers find these toothbrushes especially helpful for children with special needs such as autism or sensory issues, making brushing faster and easier.
The multi-sided bristle design cleans all tooth surfaces quickly, which reviewers appreciate for uncooperative or time-limited brushing.
Some reviewers report the bristles are too short to reach the gum line and question the overall quality.
A few reviewers note the brushes are adult-sized rather than toddler-sized, or require strength and dexterity that some users lack.
Some reviewers find the design takes getting used to or doesn't work well for their toddler.
